theorem_title: Arbitrarily long finite sequences of expanding alternating blocks
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$. Write $B=T^3$, and let $B^j$ be its j-fold iterate. A start $n$ has $m$ good blocks if $B^j(n)\equiv11\pmod{16}$ for every $j<m$.

For every natural $m>0$,

$$
\exists n\in\mathbb N,\quad (\forall j<m,\ B^j(n)\equiv11\pmod{16})\ \land\ n<B^m(n).
$$

The starting value may depend on the finite requested length. This does not assert the existence of one infinitely expanding orbit.
